name: Westfall Lighthouse
summary: Westfall Lighthouse watches over the rocky isle off Westfall's southwestern shore, its beacon dark and its keepers gone. Old Murk-Eye led the attack that killed them, and Captain Grayson's spirit remains by the tower.

sections.title: A Beacon in the Mist
sections.body: Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships along Westfall's dangerous southwestern bluffs and the coast near Stormwind. As law and order failed across the region, royal patrols dwindled and coastal dangers grew unchecked. Murloc tribes drove the lighthouse keepers inland. The family returned to relight the beacon, but Old Murk-Eye rallied his kin for another attack. The murlocs killed the keepers and put out the light.

sections.title: The Ghostly Watch
sections.body: Captain Grayson haunts the rocky outcrop beside Westfall Lighthouse. Bound to the place where he watched the keepers die, the ghost cannot rest while the beacon is dark and monsters crawl along the shore. Grayson asks passing adventurers to gather oil from the harvest golems to keep the flame burning, and to hunt Old Murk-Eye in revenge for the fallen keepers.

faq.q: Why is the Westfall Lighthouse abandoned?
faq.answer: Local murlocs drove the human family who tended Westfall Lighthouse inland. When they returned to relight the beacon, Old Murk-Eye led another attack and killed them before Captain Grayson.

Captain Grayson is a ghost who haunts the island outside Westfall Lighthouse. After witnessing the keepers' deaths, he asks travelers to gather oil to keep the beacon lit and hunt the coastal murlocs responsible.
Old Murk-Eye is a cunning, vicious murloc chieftain who stalks the Westfall shoreline. He rallied the coastal tribes to attack Westfall Lighthouse and kill its keepers.
The mechanical lantern still works, casting a beam across the ocean at night. Captain Grayson asks travelers for the oil needed to keep its flame burning.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you see how far Stormwind's reach has failed at Westfall Lighthouse. The kingdom's isolated servants were left without military support against the coastal beasts.
